steps: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this existing two-poster artwork. KEEP every illustration and all colors, pencil shapes, colored drawing trails, paper grain, composition, panel proportions and borders the same. Keep the LEFT hourglass poster unchanged, including its red ascending slash. Change ONLY the cancellation mark on the RIGHT colored-pencils poster: completely REMOVE the existing red diagonal prohibition stripe that rises from bottom-left to top-right. Restore the pencil/color artwork where that old stripe was. Replace it with ONE bold rough-brushed MATTE BLACK cancellation stripe descending from the TOP LEFT of the right poster to the BOTTOM RIGHT of the right poster. It must look like a BLACK BACKSLASH (\), NOT a forward slash (/), and not an X. On the right poster, its start is near the upper-left ivory corner above the blue pencil, its end near the lower-right corner across the red/yellow drawing trails. The black brush stripe should be as thick, forceful and readable as the previous red stripe. Keep the blue, green, yellow and red pencils and their broad colored trails vivid and recognizable; the red pencil and red colored trail remain red, only the separate prohibition mark becomes black. No old red diagonal cancellation mark should remain. Absolutely no words, letters, numerals, labels, logo or watermark. Do not modify the left poster or introduce other subjects. This is a surgical correction, not a redesign.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Make one surgical change to the provided two-poster artwork: on the RIGHT colored-pencil poster, make the existing BLACK diagonal cancellation brushstroke EXACTLY TWICE AS WIDE as it is now, measured perpendicular to the stroke. Keep the stroke centered on the same descending diagonal, from the upper LEFT corner area to the lower RIGHT corner area of the right poster (a backslash \). Keep its black color and rough hand-painted brush edges. It must be a very bold, broad opaque BLACK stripe, with approximately double the current width from end to end, including its middle. Do not add a second stroke and do not make an X. Keep all FOUR pencil colors, pencil geometry, their colored trails, paper texture, crop, proportions and layout unchanged underneath; the thicker black stroke naturally covers more of them. Keep the LEFT hourglass poster entirely unchanged including its red slash. Do not change the artwork, positions, overall image dimensions or any other detail. Absolutely no text, letters, labels, numbers or watermark. Only double the thickness of that one black stroke.
